sourcedFrom: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) (UNDATED — Beretta prints a form code rather than a year)
cleanIntro: An A400 strips without a tool: cap, fore-end, barrel, and the bolt group off the magazine tube. The gas system is the part that decides whether it keeps running — clean it, and then put it back DRY, because Beretta says these components must not be lubricated at all.

steps.title: Empty, all three places, hammer decocked
steps.action: Chamber, receiver and magazine — checked by eye through the ejection port, the loading gate and the chamber — and then check the hammer is decocked. A tube-fed gun that looks empty at the port can still be holding shells.
steps.aside: It is advisable to carry out the stripping operations over a table to catch components should they drop.
steps.quote: ALWAYS CHECK THAT THE SHOTGUN IS UNLOADED (EMPTY CARTRIDGE CHAMBER, EMPTY RECEIVER, EMPTY MAGAZINE). INSPECT THE FIREARM BY LOOKING THROUGH THE EJECTION PORT, THE LOADING GATE AND THE CHAMBER. IF IT IS NOT EMPTY, UNLOAD IT AS INSTRUCTED IN THE RELEVANT SECTION. CHECK THAT THE HAMMER IS DECOCKED.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

steps.title: Carrier stop pin DOWN, bolt locked open
steps.action: Push the carrier stop pin all the way down if it is not already, then draw the bolt fully back so it stays open. Both of those have to be true before the fore-end cap will let anything go.
steps.aside: Pull the breech bolt all the way back so that it remains open
steps.quote: Check that the carrier stop pin is pressed all the way down. If it is not, push it all the way down
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

steps.title: Fore-end cap off, fore-end forward
steps.action: Unscrew the front cap of the fore-end anticlockwise, then hold the gun by the BARREL and draw the fore-end straight out toward the muzzle.
steps.aside: Holding the shotgun by the barrel, pull the fore-end straight out toward the muzzle.
steps.quote: Unscrew the front cap of the fore-end in an anticlockwise direction.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

steps.title: ⛔ Hold the piston, draw the barrel — and leave the valve alone
steps.action: Pull the barrel out of the stock-receiver assembly while holding the piston inside the gas cylinder; release it and the piston parts come off the tube. ⛔ Then stop at the valve: never strip its spring or its retaining nut. It is self-cleaning and needs nothing, and anything genuinely wrong with it is a factory-trained gunsmith's job.
steps.aside: NEVER STRIP the spring of the valve or the valve retaining nut
steps.quote: Pull the barrel out of the stock-receiver assembly while holding the piston inside the gas cylinder.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

steps.title: Barrel, and the locking shoulders at the breech
steps.action: Soft flannel through the bore for combustion residue, bronze brush or an oiled cloth if it needs more. Then clean the LOCKING SHOULDERS on the barrel breech thoroughly — that is what the bolt locks into, and fouling there is a gun that will not close. Dry cloth through, light oil, then check the bore is clear.
steps.aside: Carefully clean the inside of the barrel with a soft cloth (flannel) to remove any combustion residue. If necessary, use a bronze brush or a cloth soaked with Beretta Gun Oil.
steps.quote: Thoroughly clean the locking shoulders on the barrel breech.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — ROUTINE MAINTENANCE, printed p.35-36

steps.title: ⛔ Magnum loads foul the gas system — and it goes back DRY
steps.action: Beretta names the parts Magnum and Super Magnum powders foul: the gas cylinder, the piston, the elastic piston seal and the magazine tube. Clean and spray them, check the piston still glides freely on the tube, brush the cylinder walls and wipe them out. ⛔ Then leave them dry — the book says these components must not be lubricated, and oil there turns residue into paste.
steps.aside: The components specified above must not be lubricated.
steps.quote: Carefully clean the piston, elastic piston seal and magazine tube and spray with Beretta Gun Oil.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — ROUTINE MAINTENANCE, printed p.35-36

steps.title: Ensure the piston still glides on the tube
steps.action: This is the functional check that matters on a gas gun: run the piston along the magazine tube by hand and feel that it moves freely. If it drags, the gun will short-stroke long before it fails to fire.
steps.aside: To clean the walls of the gas cylinder, spray them with Beretta Gun Oil and clean thoroughly with a bronze brush.
steps.quote: Ensure that the piston glides freely on the magazine tube.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — ROUTINE MAINTENANCE, printed p.35-36

deepSteps.title: Bolt strip is for cleaning only
deepSteps.action: Beretta gives the reason before the procedure: the breech bolt assembly needs only to be disassembled in order to clean its components. End of season, or after a soaking — not every outing.
deepSteps.quote: The breech bolt assembly needs only to be disassembled in order to clean its components.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

deepSteps.title: Ride the bolt forward, then depress the bolt head
deepSteps.action: Keep a finger on the cocking handle, press the release button and let the bolt run forward slowly until it stops. Then press the head of the bolt until the groove in its neck lines up with the edge of the bolt body — with that groove aligned, the handle will come out and not before.
deepSteps.aside: Keeping the head depressed in this position, extract the cocking handle from the breech bolt, pulling forcefully.
deepSteps.quote: Press the head of the breech bolt until the groove on its neck corresponds to the edge of the bolt body.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

deepSteps.title: Bolt group forward off the receiver, ejection port UP
deepSteps.action: Over a flat surface with the ejection port facing UP, pull the bolt assembly, the operating rods with sleeve, the recoil spring and the spring holder forward together to force the bolt out of the receiver. Port up keeps the firing pin, locking block and springs inside the bolt rather than on the bench.
deepSteps.quote: Working over a flat surface, with the ejection port pointed upwards, pull forward on the breech bolt assembly, the operating rods with sleeve, the recoil spring, and the spring holder, to force the breech bolt out from the receiver
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

deepSteps.title: Trigger plate out — safety ON, hammer cocked
deepSteps.action: Engage the safety with the hammer cocked, press the carrier stop pin, then drive the trigger guard retaining pin out with a punch or an awl. Lever the trigger plate out by pressing on the trigger guard, first toward the barrel and then outward. Two directions, in that order.
deepSteps.aside: The trigger plate only needs to be disassembled in order to clean the trigger mechanism.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the trigger guard retaining pin by pressing with a pin punch or an awl.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

deepSteps.title: Clean the bolt, the plate and the receiver — then stop
deepSteps.action: Spray and clean the bolt parts, dry them thoroughly and lubricate lightly. Wipe the trigger plate clean and put a light film on the metal components and the retaining pin. Do the receiver the same way. ⛔ The trigger plate comes OUT to be cleaned; it does not come APART, and the valve assembly is never disassembled at all.
deepSteps.quote: Lightly lubricate all the metal components and the trigger plate retaining pin.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — MAN0088/001 (form code printed in the running header) — SPECIAL MAINTENANCE, printed p.36

cleaning.name: BARREL & LOCKING SHOULDERS
tasks: Flannel through the bore; bronze brush if the residue needs it
Locking shoulders at the barrel breech cleaned thoroughly
Dry cloth through, then a light oil — bore checked clear

cleaning.name: GAS CYLINDER, PISTON, SEAL, MAGAZINE TUBE
tasks: Piston, elastic piston seal and magazine tube cleaned and sprayed
Piston must glide freely along the tube by hand
Cylinder walls sprayed and brushed with a bronze brush, then wiped out
⛔ These components must NOT be lubricated

cleaning.name: BREECH BOLT, TRIGGER PLATE, RECEIVER (end of season)
tasks: Bolt parts sprayed, dried thoroughly, lightly lubricated
Trigger plate wiped; metal parts and retaining pin lightly oiled
Receiver's internal bolt guides cleaned and lubricated

cleaning.name: ⛔ LEAVE ALONE
tasks: The valve assembly is never disassembled
The valve spring and retaining nut are never stripped
Never spray or apply oil to cartridges

reassembly: Bolt group, operating rods with sleeve, recoil spring and spring holder back onto the magazine tube shaft, ejection port UP on a flat surface.
Cocking handle back into the bolt with the neck groove aligned, driven fully home.
Trigger plate into the receiver and its retaining pin pressed back in.
Barrel checked clear and back into the receiver with the piston held inside its gas cylinder.
Cycle the action, confirm lock-open and return to battery, then function check.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded: cycle the bolt several times and confirm it locks open on the carrier stop and returns fully into battery. Check the fore-end cap is tight and the choke is seated. If the gun short-strokes after a clean, suspect oil left in the gas cylinder — those parts run dry by design.
